translations.idiomatic: Under the old regulations, at temple sacrifices the emperor himself led the rite, with the Grand Commandant performing the secondary libation;

sentences.zh: 南郊親奉，以太常亞獻。

translations.literal: At the southern suburban sacrifice he personally officiates, with the Minister of Ceremonies performing the secondary libation.
translations.idiomatic: at the southern suburban sacrifice he likewise officiated in person, with the Minister of Ceremonies performing the secondary libation.

sentences.zh: 又廟祠行事之始，以酒灌地；

translations.literal: Moreover, at the beginning of temple sacrifice ritual, wine is poured on the ground;
translations.idiomatic: At temple rites, moreover, the ceremony opened with pouring wine on the ground;

sentences.zh: 送神則不灌。

translations.literal: When seeing off the spirits, there is no pouring.
translations.idiomatic: but when the spirits were dismissed, no libation was poured.

sentences.zh: 而郊初灌，同之於廟，送神又灌，議儀不同，於事有疑。

translations.literal: Yet at the suburb the initial pouring is the same as at the temple, and again at seeing off the spirits there is pouring— the debated ritual differs, and in the matter there is doubt.
translations.idiomatic: At the suburban altar, libation occurred both at the opening and at the dismissal of the spirits—unlike the temple practice—raising doubts about which rite was correct.

sentences.zh: 輒下禮官詳正。

translations.literal: We have referred it down to the ritual officials for detailed correction.
translations.idiomatic: We request that the ritual officials examine and resolve these discrepancies.

sentences.zh: 」太學博士王祀之議：「案周禮，大宗伯『佐王保國，以吉禮事鬼神祇，禋祀昊天』。

translations.literal: " The Erudite of the Imperial Academy Wang Sizhi argued: "According to the Rites of Zhou, the Chief Ritualist 'assists the king in securing the state, serving ghosts, spirits, and earthly powers with auspicious ritual, performing the smoke sacrifice to August Heaven.'
translations.idiomatic: Wang Sizhi, Erudite of the Imperial Academy, argued: "The Rites of Zhou assigns the Chief Ritualist to 'assist the king in guarding the realm, serving spirits and deities through auspicious ritual, and performing the smoke sacrifice to August Heaven.'

sentences.zh: 則今太常是也。

translations.literal: Then the present Minister of Ceremonies is this.
translations.idiomatic: That office corresponds to today's Minister of Ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 以郊天，太常亞獻。

translations.literal: In sacrificing to Heaven at the suburb, the Minister of Ceremonies performs the secondary libation.
translations.idiomatic: For the suburban sacrifice to Heaven, the Minister of Ceremonies should perform the secondary libation.

sentences.zh: 又周禮外宗云：『王后不與，則贊宗伯。

translations.literal: Moreover the Rites of Zhou Outer Ceremonialist says: 'When the queen consort does not participate, then assist the Ritualist.'
translations.idiomatic: The Rites of Zhou also states, in the section on the Outer Ceremonialist: 'When the queen consort does not attend, she assists the Ritualist.

sentences.zh: 』鄭玄云：『后不與祭，宗伯攝其事。

translations.literal: " Zheng Xuan says: 'When the queen consort does not participate in sacrifice, the Ritualist takes charge of the affair.'
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Xuan explains: 'When the queen does not attend the sacrifice, the Ritualist takes charge of it.

sentences.zh: 』又說云：『君執圭瓚祼尸，大宗伯執璋瓚亞獻。

translations.literal: " Another explanation says: 'The lord holds the jade libation cup and pours for the corpse; the Chief Ritualist holds the jade libation cup on the long handle and performs the secondary libation.'
translations.idiomatic: His commentary also states: 'The ruler holds the libation cup and pours for the deceased; the Chief Ritualist holds the long-handled libation cup and performs the secondary libation.

sentences.zh: 』中代以來，后不廟祭，則應依禮大宗伯攝亞獻也。

translations.literal: " Since the middle generations, the queen consort has not sacrificed at the temple; then according to ritual the Chief Ritualist should act in her stead for the secondary libation.
translations.idiomatic: Since middle antiquity the empress no longer participated in temple sacrifices; by that logic the Chief Ritualist ought to stand in for her at the secondary libation.

sentences.zh: 而今以太尉亞獻。

translations.literal: Yet now the Grand Commandant performs the secondary libation.
translations.idiomatic: Yet in current practice the Grand Commandant performs the secondary libation.

sentences.zh: 鄭注禮月令云：『三王有司馬，無太尉。

translations.literal: Zheng's commentary on the Monthly Ordinances in the Book of Rites says: 'The Three Dynasties had the Minister of War; they had no Grand Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Xuan's commentary on the Monthly Ordinances notes: 'The Three Dynasties had a Minister of War, not a Grand Commandant.

sentences.zh: 太尉，秦官也。

translations.literal: The Grand Commandant is a Qin office.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Commandant was a Qin institution.

sentences.zh: 』蓋世代彌久，宗廟崇敬，攝后事重，故以上公亞獻。

translations.literal: " Probably as generations grew distant, reverence for the ancestral temple increased, and taking the queen's role was weighty— thus a top-tier duke performs the secondary libation.
translations.idiomatic: Over time reverence for the ancestral temple deepened, and standing in for the empress became a weighty duty—hence a senior duke was assigned the secondary libation.

sentences.zh: 」又議：「履時之思，情深於霜露；

translations.literal: " He also argued: "The thought felt when walking in season is deeper than frost and dew;
translations.idiomatic: He further argued: "The filial feeling that comes when one walks the seasons runs deeper than frost and dew;

sentences.zh: 室戶之感，有懷於容聲。

translations.literal: The feeling at the chamber door is stirred by remembered voice and appearance.
translations.idiomatic: at the door of the ancestral chamber one is moved by the echo of a familiar voice.

sentences.zh: 不知神之所在，求之不以一處。

translations.literal: Not knowing where the spirits are, one seeks them not in a single place.
translations.idiomatic: Since one cannot know where the spirits dwell, one seeks them in more than one place.

sentences.zh: 鄭注儀禮有司云，天子諸侯祭於祊而繹。

translations.literal: Zheng's commentary on the Officers section of the Ceremonial Rites says, the Son of Heaven and feudal lords sacrifice at the side altar and then perform the follow-up offering.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Xuan's commentary on the Officers section of the Ceremonial Rites states that the Son of Heaven and feudal lords offer at the side altar and then perform the follow-up sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 繹又祭也。

translations.literal: The follow-up offering is again a sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: The follow-up offering is itself another sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 今廟祠闕送神之祼，將移祭於祊繹，明在於留神，未得而殺。

translations.literal: Now at temple sacrifice the libation at seeing off the spirits is lacking; the sacrifice will be moved to the side altar follow-up offering— clearly the point is to detain the spirits, not yet able to dismiss them.
translations.idiomatic: Temple ritual today omits the farewell libation because the offering is shifted to the side-altar follow-up sacrifice—the spirits are being detained, not yet released.

sentences.zh: 禮郊廟祭殊，故灌送有異。

translations.literal: Ritual: suburban and temple sacrifices differ, thus pouring at dismissal differs.
translations.idiomatic: Suburban and temple rites differ by design, and so their libation practices at dismissal should differ as well.

sentences.zh: 」太常丞朱膺之議：「案周禮，大宗伯使掌典禮，以事神為上，職總祭祀，而昊天為首。

translations.literal: " Assistant Director of the Minister of Ceremonies Zhu Yingzhi argued: "According to the Rites of Zhou, the Chief Ritualist was made to administer canonical ritual, placing service to spirits foremost, his duty summing up sacrifices— with August Heaven first.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Yingzhi, Assistant Director of the Minister of Ceremonies, argued: "The Rites of Zhou charges the Chief Ritualist with canonical ritual, ranking service to the spirits above all else and overseeing every sacrifice—with August Heaven foremost.

sentences.zh: 今太常即宗伯也。

translations.literal: The present Minister of Ceremonies is the Ritualist.
translations.idiomatic: Today's Minister of Ceremonies is that same Chief Ritualist.

sentences.zh: 又尋袁山松漢百官志云：『郊祀之事，太尉掌亞獻，光祿掌三獻。

translations.literal: Moreover, seeking in Yuan Shunsong's Register of Han Offices it says: 'For suburban sacrifice affairs, the Grand Commandant handles the secondary libation, the Supervisor of Attendants handles the tertiary libation.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Shunsong's Register of Han Offices further records: 'At suburban sacrifices the Grand Commandant performed the secondary libation and the Supervisor of Attendants the tertiary libation.

sentences.zh: 太常每祭祀，先奏其禮儀及行事，掌贊天子。

translations.literal: The Minister of Ceremonies at each sacrifice first presents its ritual protocol and procedure, and assists the Son of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: At every sacrifice the Minister of Ceremonies reported the ritual order in advance and stood beside the emperor to assist him.

sentences.zh: 』無掌獻事。

translations.literal: " He had no charge of libation affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He had no duty of performing the libations.

sentences.zh: 如儀志，漢亞獻之事，專由上司，不由秩宗貴官也。

translations.literal: As the ritual records show, Han secondary libation affairs were exclusively the province of senior ministers, not the exalted office of the Minister of Ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: The ritual records show that in Han times secondary libation was always the province of senior ministers, not the exalted Minister of Ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 今宗廟太尉亞獻，光祿三獻，則漢儀也。

translations.literal: Now at the ancestral temple the Grand Commandant performs secondary libation and the Supervisor of Attendants tertiary libation— this is Han practice.
translations.idiomatic: Today the Grand Commandant's secondary libation and the Supervisor of Attendants' tertiary libation at the ancestral temple follow Han practice.

sentences.zh: 又賀循制太尉由東南道升壇，明此官必預郊祭。

translations.literal: Moreover He Xun's regulations have the Grand Commandant ascend the altar by the southeast path— showing this officer must participate in the suburban sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: He Xun's regulations also require the Grand Commandant to ascend the altar by the southeast ramp—clear proof that this officer must take part in the suburban sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 古禮雖由宗伯，然世有因革，上司亞獻，漢儀所行。

translations.literal: Ancient ritual was through the Ritualist, yet ages have their alterations and reforms— the senior minister's secondary libation is what Han practice carried out.
translations.idiomatic: Ancient rite may have assigned the secondary libation to the Ritualist, but custom changes with the age; the senior minister's secondary libation is what Han practice established.

sentences.zh: 愚謂郊祀禮重，宜同宗廟。

translations.literal: I consider the suburban sacrifice ritual weighty— it should match the ancestral temple.
translations.idiomatic: I believe the suburban sacrifice is no less solemn than the ancestral rites, and the two should be aligned.

sentences.zh: 且太常既掌贊天子，事不容兼。

translations.literal: Moreover the Minister of Ceremonies already assists the Son of Heaven— the office cannot accommodate both duties.
translations.idiomatic: And the Minister of Ceremonies already assists the emperor throughout the ceremony—he cannot take on a second major role.

sentences.zh: 又尋灌事，禮記曰：『祭求諸陰陽之義也。

translations.literal: Moreover seeking into libation affairs, the Book of Rites says: 'Sacrifice seeks the meaning in yin and yang.
translations.idiomatic: On the question of libation, the Book of Rites says: 'Sacrifice seeks communion between yin and yang.

sentences.zh: 殷人先求諸陽。

translations.literal: The Yin people first seek in yang.
translations.idiomatic: The Yin dynasty first sought the yang principle.

sentences.zh: 』『樂三闋然後迎牲』。

translations.literal: " 'After three movements of music then welcome the sacrificial victim.'
translations.idiomatic: 'After three movements of music, the victim was brought in.

sentences.zh: 則殷人後灌也。

translations.literal: Then the Yin people poured libation afterward.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the Yin people poured the libation only after that.

sentences.zh: 『周人先求諸陰』，『灌用鬯。

translations.literal: 'The Zhou people first seek in yin,' 'libation uses fragrant wine.
translations.idiomatic: 'The Zhou people first sought the yin principle.' 'Libation used fragrant wine,

sentences.zh: 達於淵泉。

translations.literal: Reaching to the deep springs.
translations.idiomatic: reaching down to the deep springs.

sentences.zh: 既灌，然後迎牲』。

translations.literal: After libation, then welcome the sacrificial victim.'
translations.idiomatic: 'Only after the libation was the victim brought in.

sentences.zh: 則周人先灌也。

translations.literal: Then the Zhou people poured libation first.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the Zhou people poured libation first.

sentences.zh: 此謂廟祭，非謂郊祠。

translations.literal: This refers to temple sacrifice, not to suburban rite.
translations.idiomatic: All of this concerns temple sacrifice, not the suburban rite.

sentences.zh: 案周禮天官：『凡祭祀贊王祼將之事。

translations.literal: According to the Rites of Zhou, Heavenly Offices: 'For all sacrifices, assist the king in libation and offering affairs.'
translations.idiomatic: The Heavenly Offices section of the Rites of Zhou states: 'At all sacrifices, assist the king in libation and offering.

sentences.zh: 』鄭注云：『祼者，灌也。

translations.literal: " Zheng's commentary says: 'Libation means pouring.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Xuan explains: 'Libation (guan) means pouring (guan).

sentences.zh: 唯人道宗廟有灌，天地大神至尊不灌。

translations.literal: Only the human way of the ancestral temple has libation pouring; Heaven and Earth, the great spirits most exalted, receive no libation pouring.
translations.idiomatic: Only human ancestors in the temple receive poured libations; Heaven and Earth, supreme among spirits, do not.

sentences.zh: 』而郊未始有灌，於禮未詳。

translations.literal: " Yet at the suburban sacrifice there was never libation pouring— from ritual it is unclear.
translations.idiomatic: Suburban sacrifice never included libation in the first place, so its presence in current practice is ritually dubious.

sentences.zh: 淵儒注義，炳然明審。

translations.literal: The deep scholars' annotated meanings are brilliantly clear and detailed.
translations.idiomatic: The commentaries of the great ritual scholars leave no doubt.

sentences.zh: 謂今之有灌，相承為失，則宜無灌。

translations.literal: I say that the present having libation pouring, handed down as error, then there should be no libation pouring.
translations.idiomatic: If the libations now performed are an inherited error, they should be abolished.

sentences.zh: 」通關八座丞郎博士，並同膺之議。

translations.literal: " Referred to all Eight Ministers, assistant directors, gentlemen, and erudites— all agreed with Yingzhi's proposal.
translations.idiomatic: The matter was circulated among the Eight Ministers, their assistants, gentlemen, and erudites, and all endorsed Zhu Yingzhi's view.

sentences.zh: 尚書令建平王宏重參議，謂膺之議為允。

translations.literal: The Director of the Masters of Writing, Prince of Pingjian Hong, again joined deliberation and judged Yingzhi's proposal acceptable.
translations.idiomatic: The Director of the Masters of Writing, Prince Liu Hong of Pingjian, reviewed the debate again and found Zhu Yingzhi's proposal acceptable.

sentences.zh: 詔可。

translations.literal: The edict approved.
translations.idiomatic: An edict approved it.

sentences.zh: 大明二年正月丙午朔，有司奏：「今月六日南郊，輿駕親奉。

translations.literal: On the first day bingwu of the first month of Daming year two, the responsible officials memorialized: "On the sixth of this month is the southern suburban sacrifice; the imperial carriage will personally officiate.
translations.idiomatic: On the new moon of the first month of Daming 2, the responsible officials submitted: "The southern suburban sacrifice falls on the sixth of this month, and the emperor will officiate in person.

sentences.zh: 至時或雨。

translations.literal: At the time there may be rain.
translations.idiomatic: Rain may fall on that day.

sentences.zh: 魏世值雨，高堂隆謂應更用後辛。

translations.literal: In Wei times when rain occurred, Gao Tanglong said one should again use the next xin day.
translations.idiomatic: Under Wei, when rain fell, Gao Tanglong argued that the rite should be moved to the next xin day.

sentences.zh: 晉時既出遇雨，顧和亦云宜更告。

translations.literal: In Jin times when they had set out and encountered rain, Gu He also said one should again announce.
translations.idiomatic: In Jin, when the procession had already set out and met rain, Gu He likewise held that a fresh announcement was required.

sentences.zh: 徐禪云：『晉武之世，或用丙，或用己，或用庚。

translations.literal: Xu Chan says: 'In the reign of Emperor Wu of Jin, sometimes day bing was used, sometimes day ji, sometimes day geng.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Chan notes that under Emperor Wu of Jin, make-up dates sometimes fell on bing days, sometimes on ji or geng days.

sentences.zh: 』使禮官議正并詳。

translations.literal: " Have the ritual officials deliberate and correct, and explain in detail.
translations.idiomatic: We ask the ritual officials to settle these questions in full.

sentences.zh: 若得遷日，應更告廟與不？

translations.literal: If the date can be moved, should one again announce to the temple or not?
translations.idiomatic: If the date is postponed, must the ancestral temple be notified again?

sentences.zh: 」博士王燮之議稱：「遇雨遷郊，則先代成議。

translations.literal: " Erudite Wang Xiezhi argued: "When rain forces postponement of the suburban sacrifice, former generations established precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xiezhi, Erudite of the Academy, argued: "Postponing the suburban sacrifice because of rain was settled practice in earlier dynasties.

sentences.zh: 禮傳所記，辛日有徵。

translations.literal: What the ritual texts record gives evidence for xin days.
translations.idiomatic: The ritual classics also provide clear precedent for xin days.

sentences.zh: 郊特牲曰：『郊之用辛也，周之始郊日以至。

translations.literal: Suburban Sacrifice Special Beast says: 'The suburb uses xin day; Zhou's first suburban sacrifice day arrived accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: The Suburban Sacrifice chapter states: 'The suburban rite uses a xin day; when Zhou first performed it, the season had just arrived.

sentences.zh: 』鄭玄注曰：『三王之郊，一用夏正。

translations.literal: " Zheng Xuan annotates: 'The Three Dynasties' suburban sacrifices all use the Xia calendar's first month.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Xuan explains: 'All three dynasties held their suburban sacrifices in the first month of the Xia calendar.

sentences.zh: 用辛者，取其齋戒自新也。

translations.literal: Using xin is to take its fasting and purification, self-renewal.
translations.idiomatic: They chose xin days for their associations with fasting, purification, and renewal.

sentences.zh: 』又月令曰：『乃擇元日，祈穀于上帝。

translations.literal: " Moreover Monthly Ordinances says: 'Then select the primal day, pray for grain to the Supreme Lord.
translations.idiomatic: The Monthly Ordinances also commands: 'Choose the primal day and pray for grain to the Supreme Lord.

sentences.zh: 』注曰：『元日，謂上辛。

translations.literal: " Commentary says: 'Primal day means the upper xin.
translations.idiomatic: The commentary defines 'primal day' as the first xin day of the month.

sentences.zh: 郊祭天也。

translations.literal: Suburban sacrifice is sacrifice to Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: The suburban sacrifice is the rite of Heaven.

sentences.zh: 』又春秋載郊有二，成十七年九月辛丑，郊。

translations.literal: " Moreover Spring and Autumn records two suburban sacrifices: seventeenth year of Duke Cheng, ninth month, day xinchou, suburban sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: The Spring and Autumn Annals records two suburban sacrifices: in Duke Cheng's seventeenth year, on xinchou day of the ninth month;

sentences.zh: 公羊曰：『曷用郊？

translations.literal: Gongyang says: 'Why use the suburban sacrifice?
translations.idiomatic: and in the Gongyang commentary: 'Why hold a suburban sacrifice?

sentences.zh: 用正月上辛。

translations.literal: Use the upper xin of the first month.
translations.idiomatic: On the first xin of the first month.

sentences.zh: 』哀元年四月辛巳，郊。

translations.literal: " First year of Duke Ai, fourth month, day xinsi, suburban sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: In Duke Ai's first year, on xinsi day of the fourth month, again a suburban sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 穀梁曰：『自正月至于三月，郊之時也。

translations.literal: Guliang says: 'From the first month until the third month is the time for the suburban sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: The Guliang commentary explains: 'From the first month through the third month is the season for the suburban sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 以十二月下辛卜正月上辛。

translations.literal: On the lower xin of the twelfth month divine the upper xin of the first month.
translations.idiomatic: On the last xin of the twelfth month one divined the first xin of the first month;

sentences.zh: 如不從，以正月下辛卜二月上辛。

translations.literal: If not accepted, on the lower xin of the first month divine the upper xin of the second month.
translations.idiomatic: if Heaven did not approve, one divined again from the last xin of the first month toward the first xin of the second;

sentences.zh: 如不從，以二月下辛卜三月上辛。

translations.literal: If not accepted, on the lower xin of the second month divine the upper xin of the third month.
translations.idiomatic: and if still not approved, from the last xin of the second month toward the first xin of the third.

sentences.zh: 』以斯明之，則郊祭之禮，未有不用辛日者也。

translations.literal: " By this to make clear, then the ritual of suburban sacrifice— never has there been one that did not use xin day.
translations.idiomatic: From this it is clear that the suburban sacrifice was never performed except on a xin day.

sentences.zh: 晉氏或丙、或己、或庚，並有別議。

translations.literal: The Jin house sometimes used bing, sometimes ji, sometimes geng— all had separate deliberations.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jin dynasty used bing, ji, or geng days instead, each case rested on special arguments.

sentences.zh: 武帝以十二月丙寅南郊受禪，斯則不得用辛也。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu at the southern suburban sacrifice in the twelfth month on day bingyin received the abdication— thus one could not use xin.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu received the abdication at the southern suburban altar on bingyin day in the twelfth month, that was plainly not a xin day.

sentences.zh: 又泰始二年十一月己卯，始并圓丘方澤二至之祀合於二郊。

translations.literal: Moreover in the eleventh month of Taishi year two, on day jimao, they first combined the Round Mound and Square Pond solstice sacrifices of the two extremes into the two suburban sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: In Taishi 2, on jimao day of the eleventh month, the court first merged the Round Mound and Square Pond solstice rites into the two suburban sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 三年十一月庚寅冬至祠天，郊于圓丘。

translations.literal: In year three, eleventh month, day gengyin, at the winter solstice they sacrificed to Heaven, performing the suburban sacrifice at the Round Mound.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year, on gengyin day of the eleventh month at the winter solstice, Heaven was worshipped with a suburban sacrifice at the Round Mound.

sentences.zh: 是猶用圓丘之禮，非專祈穀之祭，故又不得用辛也。

translations.literal: This still used the Round Mound ritual, not solely the prayer-for-grain sacrifice— thus again one could not use xin.
translations.idiomatic: That ceremony followed the Round Mound rite, not the spring prayer-for-grain sacrifice alone, so again a xin day was not required.

sentences.zh: 今之郊饗，既行夏時，雖得遷却，謂宜猶必用辛也。

translations.literal: Today's suburban feast, already observing the Xia calendar, though the date may be moved back— I say it is still suitable to must use xin.
translations.idiomatic: Today's suburban feast follows the Xia calendar; even if the date is postponed, a xin day should still be used.

sentences.zh: 徐禪所據，或為未宜。

translations.literal: What Xu Chan relied on may perhaps not be suitable.
translations.idiomatic: The precedents Xu Chan cited may not apply here.

sentences.zh: 又案郊特牲曰：『受命于祖廟，作龜于禰宮。

translations.literal: Moreover considering Suburban Sacrifice Special Beast: 'Receiving mandate at the ancestral temple, making tortoise divination at the father temple.'
translations.idiomatic: The Suburban Sacrifice chapter also states: "Receive the mandate at the ancestral temple and perform tortoise divination at the temple of the immediate ancestor."

sentences.zh: 』鄭玄注曰：『受命，謂告退而卜也。

translations.literal: Zheng Xuan annotates: 'Receiving mandate means announcing withdrawal and then divining.'
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Xuan explains: "'Receiving the mandate' means announcing one's departure from the ancestral temple and then divining."

sentences.zh: 』則告義在郊，非為告日。

translations.literal: Then the meaning of announcement concerns the suburban sacrifice, not announcing the day.
translations.idiomatic: The announcement concerns the suburban rite itself, not the chosen date.

sentences.zh: 今日雖有遷，而郊祀不異，愚謂不宜重告。

translations.literal: Though the day has a change, the suburban sacrifice is not different— I consider it unsuitable to announce again.
translations.idiomatic: Although the date has changed, the suburban sacrifice itself is unchanged; I do not think a second announcement is warranted.

sentences.zh: 」曹郎朱膺之議：「案先儒論郊，其議不一。

translations.literal: Section Director Zhu Yingzhi argued: "Considering the former scholars' discussions of the suburb, their opinions are not uniform.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Yingzhi, Section Director of the Ministry of Ceremonies, argued: "Earlier scholars disagreed on the suburban sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 周禮有冬至日圓丘之祭。

translations.literal: The Rites of Zhou has the Round Mound sacrifice on the winter solstice day.
translations.idiomatic: The Rites of Zhou prescribes a Round Mound sacrifice on the winter solstice.

sentences.zh: 月令孟春有祈穀于上帝。

translations.literal: The Monthly Ordinances in early spring has prayer for grain to the Supreme Lord.
translations.idiomatic: The Monthly Ordinances calls for praying for grain to the Supreme Lord in early spring.

sentences.zh: 鄭氏說，圓丘祀昊天上帝，以帝嚳配，所謂禘也。

translations.literal: Master Zheng's explanation: the Round Mound sacrifices to August Heaven the Supreme Lord, with Emperor Ku as associate— what is called di.
translations.idiomatic: In Zheng Xuan's view, the Round Mound rite worships August Heaven the Supreme Lord with Emperor Ku as associate—the great seasonal di sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 祈穀祀五精之帝，以后稷配，所謂郊也。

translations.literal: Prayer for grain sacrifices to the Five Essence Emperors, with Hou Ji as associate— what is called the suburb.
translations.idiomatic: The prayer-for-grain rite worships the Five Essence Emperors with Hou Ji as associate—the suburban sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 二祭異時，其神不同。

translations.literal: The two sacrifices are at different times; their spirits differ.
translations.idiomatic: The two ceremonies fall at different seasons and honor different deities.

sentences.zh: 諸儒云，圓丘之祭，以后稷配。

translations.literal: Various scholars say, the Round Mound sacrifice has Hou Ji as associate.
translations.idiomatic: Other scholars hold that Hou Ji served as associate at the Round Mound sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 取其所在，名之曰郊。

translations.literal: Taking its location, naming it the suburb.
translations.idiomatic: Because it was held in the suburban fields, it was called the suburban sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 以形體言之，謂之圓丘。

translations.literal: Speaking of its physical form, calling it Round Mound.
translations.idiomatic: In terms of its physical form, it was called the Round Mound.

sentences.zh: 名雖有二，其實一祭。

translations.literal: Though the names are two, in substance it is one sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: The names differ, but in substance it is one sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 晉武捨鄭而從諸儒，是以郊用冬至日。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Jin abandoned Zheng and followed the various scholars— thus the suburb used the winter solstice day.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Jin rejected Zheng Xuan's view and followed other scholars, hence the suburban sacrifice fell on the winter solstice.

sentences.zh: 既以至日，理無常辛。

translations.literal: Since it was at the solstice day, by principle there is no fixed xin.
translations.idiomatic: Because the date was fixed by the solstice, there was no constant xin-day rule.

sentences.zh: 然則晉代中原不用辛日郊，如徐禪議也。

translations.literal: Thus in Jin times in the Central Plains xin day was not used for the suburb— as in Xu Chan's proposal.
translations.idiomatic: Jin practice in the Central Plains thus did not require xin days for the suburb, just as Xu Chan argued.

sentences.zh: 江左以來，皆用正月，當以傳云三王之郊，各以其正，晉不改正朔，行夏之時，故因以首歲，不以冬日，皆用上辛，近代成典也。

translations.literal: Since Jiangzuo, all use the first month— it should be because the tradition says the Three Dynasties' suburban sacrifices each use their first month; Jin did not change the calendar inauguration, observing the Xia seasons— thus following the year's beginning, not the winter day, all use the upper xin— a recent established canon.
translations.idiomatic: South of the Yangzi, the sacrifice has been held in the first month since Jin moved east: the classics say each dynasty's suburban rite used its own New Year month; the court kept the Xia calendar, so the rite follows the year's opening rather than the winter solstice, always on the first xin—a practice now entrenched as law.

sentences.zh: 夫祭之禮，『過時不舉』。

translations.literal: As for sacrifice ritual, 'once the season passes, do not perform it.'
translations.idiomatic: Ritual prescribes that a sacrifice not performed in season should not be held later.

sentences.zh: 今在孟春，郊時未過，值雨遷日，於禮無違。

translations.literal: Now in early spring, the suburban season has not passed; encountering rain and moving the day— in ritual there is no violation.
translations.idiomatic: We are still in early spring, within the proper season; postponing because of rain violates no rule.

sentences.zh: 既已告日，而以事不從，禋祀重敬，謂宜更告。

translations.literal: Having already announced the day, yet the affair did not proceed— the smoke sacrifice values reverence; I say one should announce again.
translations.idiomatic: Once the date has been announced, reverence requires a fresh announcement if the rite cannot proceed.

sentences.zh: 高堂隆云：『九日南郊，十日北郊。

translations.literal: Gao Tanglong says: 'Ninth day southern suburb, tenth day northern suburb.'
translations.idiomatic: Gao Tanglong records the southern suburb on the ninth day and the northern suburb on the tenth.

sentences.zh: 』是為北郊可不以辛也。

translations.literal: This shows the northern suburb need not use xin.
translations.idiomatic: That precedent shows the northern suburban sacrifice need not fall on a xin day.

sentences.zh: 」尚書何偃議：「鄭玄注禮記，引易說三王之郊，一用夏正。

translations.literal: Director of the Masters of Writing He Yan argued: "Zheng Xuan annotating the Book of Rites cites the Changes explanation that the Three Dynasties' suburban sacrifices all use the Xia calendar's first month.
translations.idiomatic: He Yan, Director of the Masters of Writing, argued: "Zheng Xuan's commentary on the Book of Rites cites the Book of Changes: all three dynasties held their suburban sacrifices in the first month of the Xia calendar.

sentences.zh: 周禮，凡國大事，多用正歲。

translations.literal: Rites of Zhou: for all great affairs of state, mostly use the proper year's beginning.
translations.idiomatic: The Rites of Zhou likewise schedules most great state affairs for the New Year month.

sentences.zh: 左傳又啟蟄而郊。

translations.literal: Zuo Commentary also has performing the suburb at the Excited Insects.
translations.idiomatic: The Zuo Commentary records a suburban sacrifice at the Excited Insects season.

sentences.zh: 則鄭之此說，誠有據矣。

translations.literal: Then Zheng's this explanation truly has basis.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Xuan's position is well grounded.

sentences.zh: 眾家異議，或云三王各用其正郊天，此蓋曲學之辯，於禮無取。

translations.literal: Various schools differ— some say the Three Kings each used their own first month to sacrifice to Heaven at the suburb— this is probably pedantic disputation, of no use for ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Dissenting views hold that each dynasty sacrificed to Heaven in its own New Year month—but that is pedantic disputation, useless for establishing ritual practice.

sentences.zh: 固知穀梁三春皆可郊之月，真所謂膚淺也。

translations.literal: Certainly knowing Guliang's that all three spring months can be suburb months— truly what is called shallow.
translations.idiomatic: As for Guliang's claim that any of the three spring months will serve, that is plainly superficial.

sentences.zh: 然用辛之說，莫不必同。

translations.literal: Yet on the explanation of using xin, none fail to agree.
translations.idiomatic: On the requirement of xin days, however, all commentators agree.

sentences.zh: 晉郊庚己，參差未見前徵。

translations.literal: Jin suburbs on geng and ji days— irregular, no prior evidence seen.
translations.idiomatic: Jin's use of geng and ji days is irregular and lacks earlier precedent.

sentences.zh: 愚謂宜從晉遷郊依禮用辛。

translations.literal: I consider it suitable to follow Jin in moving the suburb and according to ritual use xin.
translations.idiomatic: When postponing the suburban sacrifice, I hold that a xin day should still be chosen according to ritual.

sentences.zh: 燮之以受命作龜，知告不在日，學之密也。

translations.literal: Xiezhi with receiving mandate and making tortoise knows announcement is not about the day— the density of his learning.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xiezhi's reading of "receiving the mandate" and tortoise divination shows that announcements concern the rite, not the date—a finely learned point.

sentences.zh: 」右丞徐爰議以為：「郊祀用辛，有礙遷日，禮官祠曹，考詳已備。

translations.literal: Right Assistant Director Xu Ai argued: "Using xin for the suburban sacrifice impedes moving the day; the ritual officials and sacrificial bureau have examined and explained fully.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Ai, Right Assistant Director, argued: "Insisting on xin days complicates postponement; the ritual and sacrificial offices have already examined the matter thoroughly.

sentences.zh: 何偃據禮，不應重告，愚情所同。

translations.literal: He Yan according to ritual should not announce again— my humble sentiment agrees.
translations.idiomatic: He Yan is right that ritual does not require a second announcement, and I share that view.

sentences.zh: 尋告郊剋辰，於今宜改，告事而已。

translations.literal: Seeking announcement of the suburban day determined— for now should change, announcing the affair only.
translations.idiomatic: The announcement should report only the rescheduled date of the suburban sacrifice, not the entire rite anew.

sentences.zh: 次辛十日，居然展齋，養牲在滌，無緣三月。

translations.literal: The next xin day is ten days hence— plainly extending fasting, keeping victims in the pen— no cause for three months.
translations.idiomatic: The next xin day falls ten days off; fasting can begin at once and the sacrificial animals remain in the cleansing pen— there is no reason to wait until the third month.

sentences.zh: 謂毛血告牷之後，雖有事礙，便應有司行事，不容遷郊。

translations.literal: I say after announcing with blood and hair of the victim, though there is an impediment to the affair, then the responsible officials should conduct the ritual— not permitting moving the suburb.
translations.idiomatic: After the blood-and-hair announcement for the chosen victim, if rain intervenes, the responsible officials should complete the rite on the spot—the suburban sacrifice must not be moved again.

sentences.zh: 」眾議不同。

translations.literal: The various opinions differ.
translations.idiomatic: The deliberations remained divided.

sentences.zh: 參議：「宜依經，遇雨遷用後辛，不重告。

translations.literal: Joint deliberation: "It is suitable to follow the classics— when rain occurs move to the next xin, do not announce again.
translations.idiomatic: The joint recommendation: "Follow the classics—when rain forces postponement, use the next xin day without a fresh announcement.

sentences.zh: 若殺牲薦血之後值雨，則有司行事。

translations.literal: If after killing the victim and presenting blood rain occurs, then the responsible officials conduct the ritual.
translations.idiomatic: If rain falls after the victim has been slaughtered and the blood offered, the responsible officials should proceed with the ceremony."

sentences.zh: 」詔可。

translations.literal: The edict approved.
translations.idiomatic: An edict approved it.

sentences.zh: 明帝泰始二年十一月辛酉，詔曰：「朕載新寶命，仍離多難，戎車遄駕，經略務殷，禋告雖備，弗獲親禮。

translations.literal: Emperor Ming, Taishi year two eleventh month xinyou, edict: "I have newly received the precious mandate, yet still apart from many hardships; war chariots swiftly driven, strategy and planning affairs abundant— smoke announcements though complete, I did not obtain personally to perform the ritual.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of Taishi 2, Emperor Ming issued an edict: "I have newly received the imperial mandate amid unending hardship; chariots have raced to war and strategy has consumed every hour. Announcements to Heaven have been made, yet I have not worshipped in person.

sentences.zh: 今九服既康，百祀咸秩，宜聿遵前典，郊謁上帝。

translations.literal: Now the nine domains are at peace, the hundred sacrifices all in order— it is suitable to follow the former canon, at the suburb to visit the Supreme Lord.
translations.idiomatic: Now that the realm is at peace and every sacrifice restored to order, I should follow ancient precedent and perform the suburban sacrifice to worship the Supreme Lord."

sentences.zh: 」有司奏檢，未有先准。

translations.literal: Responsible officials memorialized checking— no prior standard exists.
translations.idiomatic: The responsible officials searched the records and found no exact precedent.

sentences.zh: 黃門侍郎徐爰議：「虞稱肆類，殷述昭告。

translations.literal: Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gate Xu Ai argued: "Yu spoke of performing the border sacrifice, Yin recounted the bright announcement.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Ai, Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gate, argued: "Yu performed the border sacrifice; the Yin dynasty recorded the solemn announcement to Heaven.

sentences.zh: 蓋以創世成功，德盛業遠，開統肇基，必享上帝。

translations.literal: Probably because founding the age and completing merit, virtue abundant and enterprise far-reaching, opening the succession and beginning the foundation— one must offer to the Supreme Lord.
translations.idiomatic: When a dynasty establishes itself through great achievement, its virtue and enterprise are such that it must offer worship to the Supreme Lord.

sentences.zh: 漢、魏以來，聿遵斯典。

translations.literal: From Han and Wei onward, they have followed this canon.
translations.idiomatic: From Han and Wei onward, every new reign has followed this precedent.

sentences.zh: 高祖武皇帝克伐偽楚，晉安帝尚在江陵，即於京師告義功于郊兆。

translations.literal: Grand Ancestor Emperor Wu conquered and attacked the false Chu; Emperor An of Jin was still at Jiangling— immediately at the capital he announced righteous merit at the suburban precinct.
translations.idiomatic: When Grand Ancestor Emperor Wu defeated the puppet state of Chu while Emperor An of Jin remained at Jiangling, he announced the righteous triumph at the suburban altar in the capital.

sentences.zh: 伏惟泰始應符，神武英斷，王赫出討，戎戒淹時，雖司奉弗虧，親謁尚闕。

translations.literal: Respectfully considering Taishi received the tally, divine martial and heroic in decision; the king marched forth in wrath to subdue, military vigilance prolonged— though the responsible offices' offerings were not deficient, personal audience is still lacking.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty's Taishi reign received Heaven's mandate through divine martial resolve; you marched in royal wrath while war dragged on. The responsible offices maintained the offerings, but you have not yet worshipped in person.

sentences.zh: 謹尋晉武郊以二月，晉元禋以三月。

translations.literal: Respectfully seeking, Emperor Wu of Jin performed the suburb in the second month; Emperor Yuan performed the smoke sacrifice in the third month.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Jin held his suburban sacrifice in the second month; Emperor Yuan performed the smoke sacrifice in the third.

sentences.zh: 有非常之慶，必有非常之典，不得拘以常祀，限以正月上辛。

translations.literal: Having extraordinary celebration, there must be extraordinary ceremony— one cannot be bound by ordinary sacrifice, limited to the upper xin of the first month.
translations.idiomatic: An extraordinary triumph calls for an extraordinary ceremony; it cannot be forced into the usual schedule of the first xin of the first month.

sentences.zh: 愚謂宜下史官，考擇十一月嘉吉，車駕親郊，奉謁昊天上帝，高祖武皇帝配饗。

translations.literal: I consider it suitable to refer to the historiographers, examine and select an auspicious day in the eleventh month; the imperial carriage personally at the suburb, reverently visiting August Heaven the Supreme Lord, with Grand Ancestor Emperor Wu as associate in the feast.
translations.idiomatic: I propose that the historiographers choose an auspicious day in the eleventh month for Your Majesty to conduct the suburban sacrifice in person, worshipping August Heaven the Supreme Lord with Grand Ancestor Emperor Wu as associate at the feast.

sentences.zh: 其餘祔食，不關今祭。

translations.literal: The remaining collateral offerings are not relevant to this present sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: The other collateral spirit tablets need not be included in this ceremony.

sentences.zh: 」尚書令建安王休仁等同爰議。

translations.literal: Director of the Masters of Writing Prince Xiuren of Jian'an and others agreed with Ai's proposal.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Liu Xiuren of Jian'an, Director of the Masters of Writing, and others endorsed Xu's proposal.

sentences.zh: 參議為允。

translations.literal: Joint deliberation judged it acceptable.
translations.idiomatic: The joint deliberation found it acceptable.

sentences.zh: 詔可。

translations.literal: The edict approved.
translations.idiomatic: An edict approved it.

sentences.zh: 泰始六年正月乙亥，詔曰：「古禮王者每歲郊享，爰及明堂。

translations.literal: Taishi year six first month yihai, edict: "Ancient ritual: the king each year suburban feast, extending to the Bright Hall.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of Taishi 6, an edict declared: "Ancient ritual called for the king to hold the suburban feast every year, and also to worship at the Bright Hall.

sentences.zh: 自晉以來，間年一郊，明堂同日。

translations.literal: From Jin onward, every other year one suburb, Bright Hall same day.
translations.idiomatic: From Jin onward the court sacrificed at the suburbs every other year and held the Bright Hall ceremony on the same day.

sentences.zh: 質文詳略，疏數有分。

translations.literal: Substance and ornament, detail and brevity, sparse and frequent have distinction.
translations.idiomatic: Plain and ornate forms, full and abbreviated rites, and their frequency all had their proper balance.

sentences.zh: 自今可間二年一郊，間歲一明堂。

translations.literal: From now may every other two years one suburb, every other year one Bright Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth the suburban sacrifice shall be held every two years and the Bright Hall rite every other year.

sentences.zh: 外可詳議。

translations.literal: Outside may deliberate in detail.
translations.idiomatic: The ministries may deliberate the details."

sentences.zh: 」有司奏：「前兼曹郎虞愿議：『郊祭宗祀，俱主天神，而同日殷薦，於義為黷。

translations.literal: Responsible officials memorialized: "Former Concurrent Section Director Yu Yuan proposed: 'Suburban sacrifice and ancestral worship both chiefly honor the Heavenly Spirit, yet on the same day abundant offering— in meaning it is excessive.'
translations.idiomatic: The responsible officials reported: "Yu Yuan, former Concurrent Section Director, had argued: 'The suburban sacrifice and Bright Hall worship both honor heavenly spirits; holding both with full offerings on the same day is ritually excessive.'

sentences.zh: 明詔使圓丘報功，三載一享。

translations.literal: The bright edict makes the Round Mound report merit, once every three years a feast.
translations.idiomatic: Your edict would have the Round Mound report merit with a feast every three years,

sentences.zh: 明堂配帝，間歲昭薦。

translations.literal: Bright Hall with the Emperor as associate, every other year a bright offering.
translations.idiomatic: and the Bright Hall honor the Emperor as associate with a solemn offering every other year.

sentences.zh: 詳辰酌衷，實允懋典。

translations.literal: Examining the times and weighing the mean— truly permitting the splendid canon.
translations.idiomatic: Weighing the calendar carefully, this would be a worthy and splendid arrangement."

sentences.zh: 』緣諮參議並同。

translations.literal: Referring for joint deliberation, all agreed.
translations.idiomatic: On referral for joint deliberation, all agreed.

sentences.zh: 曹郎王延秀重議：『改革之宜，實如聖旨。

translations.literal: Section Director Wang Yanxiu again argued: 'The suitability of the reform truly accords with the sage's intent.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yanxiu, Section Director, argued further: "The reform is indeed as Your Majesty intends.

sentences.zh: 前虞愿議，蓋是仰述而已，未顯後例。

translations.literal: Former Yu Yuan's proposal was probably only echoing upward— not showing the subsequent pattern.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Yuan's earlier proposal echoed Your Majesty's intent but did not spell out the resulting cycle.

sentences.zh: 謹尋自初郊間二載，明堂間一年，第二郊與第三明堂，還復同歲。

translations.literal: Respectfully seeking, from the first: suburb every two years, Bright Hall every one year— the second suburb and third Bright Hall again fall in the same year.
translations.idiomatic: Under the proposed schedule, the suburban sacrifice would come every two years and the Bright Hall every year—so the second suburban sacrifice and the third Bright Hall ceremony would again fall in the same year.

sentences.zh: 愿謂自始郊明堂以後，宜各間二年。

translations.literal: Yuan considers from the first suburb and Bright Hall onward, each should be every two years apart.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Yuan therefore proposed that after the initial ceremonies, both rites should be spaced two years apart,

sentences.zh: 以斯相推，長得異歲。

translations.literal: Pushing forward by this, always obtaining different years.
translations.idiomatic: which by extension would keep the two ceremonies on separate years indefinitely."

sentences.zh: 』通關八座，同延秀議。」

translations.literal: Referred to all Eight Ministers— agreed with Yanxiu's proposal."
translations.idiomatic: The matter was circulated among the Eight Ministers, who endorsed Wang Yanxiu's proposal."

sentences.zh: 後廢帝元徽二年十月丁巳，有司奏郊祀明堂，還復同日，間年一修。

translations.literal: Deposed Emperor, Yuanhui year two tenth month dingsi, responsible officials memorialized suburban sacrifice and Bright Hall— again same day, every other year one performance.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of Yuanhui 2 under the Deposed Emperor, the responsible officials reported that the suburban sacrifice and Bright Hall worship would again be held on the same day, once every other year.

sentences.zh: 漢文帝初祭地祇於渭陽，以高帝配，武帝立后土社祠於汾陰，亦以高帝配。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen of Han at first sacrificed to the Earth Spirit at Weiyang, with Emperor Gaozu as associate; Emperor Wu established the Queen Earth altar sacrifice at Fenyin, also with Emperor Gaozu as associate.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen of Han first sacrificed to the Earth Spirit at Weiyang with Emperor Gaozu as associate; Emperor Wu established the Queen Earth altar at Fenyin, also with Gaozu as associate.

sentences.zh: 漢氏以太祖兼配天地，則未以后配地也。

translations.literal: The Han house used the Grand Ancestor for both Heaven and Earth as associate— thus they did not yet use the empress as associate for Earth.
translations.idiomatic: The Han used the Grand Ancestor as associate for both Heaven and Earth and did not yet assign an empress to accompany Earth.

sentences.zh: 王莽作相，引周禮享先妣為配北郊。

translations.literal: Wang Mang as chancellor cited the Rites of Zhou honoring the deceased mother as associate at the northern suburb.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Mang was chancellor, he cited the Rites of Zhou to justify honoring the deceased mother as associate at the northern suburban sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 夏至祭后土，以高后配，自此始也。

translations.literal: At the summer solstice sacrificing to Queen Earth, with Empress Gaohou as associate— from this it began.
translations.idiomatic: Sacrificing to Queen Earth at the summer solstice with Empress Gaohou as associate began at that point.

sentences.zh: 光武建武中，不立北郊，故后地之祇，常配食天壇，山川羣望皆在營內，凡一千五百一十四神。

translations.literal: Guangwu in the Jianwu period did not establish the northern suburb— thus the Queen Earth spirit regularly received collateral feasting at the Heavenly Altar; mountains, rivers, and all supplicated spirits were all within the precinct, totaling 1,514 spirits.
translations.idiomatic: During Guangwu's Jianwu reign no northern suburban altar was established, so Queen Earth regularly received collateral offerings at the Heavenly Altar; mountains, rivers, and all petitioned spirits—1,514 in all—were worshipped within the same precinct.

sentences.zh: 中元年，建北郊，使司空馮魴告高廟，以薄后代呂后配地。

translations.literal: Zhongyuan year one, established northern suburb; sent Minister of Works Feng Fang to announce at the Gaozu temple, using Empress Bo to replace Empress Lü as associate for Earth.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhongyuan 1 the northern suburban altar was established; Minister of Works Feng Fang was sent to announce at the Gaozu temple, and Empress Bo replaced Empress Lü as Earth's associate.

sentences.zh: 江左初，未立北壇，地祇眾神，共在天郊也。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jiangzuo, the northern altar was not established; Earth Spirit and numerous spirits all shared the Heavenly suburban sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: When the court moved south, no northern altar existed at first; Earth and the other earth spirits were worshipped together at the heavenly suburban sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 晉成帝立二郊，天郊則六十二神，五帝之佐、日月五星、二十八宿、文昌、北斗、三台、司命、軒轅、后土、太一、天一、太微、鈎陳、北極、雨師、雷、電、司空、風伯、老人六十二神也。

translations.literal: Emperor Cheng of Jin established the two suburbs; the Heavenly suburb has 62 spirits—the Five Emperors' assistants, sun moon five stars, twenty-eight lodges, Literary Glory, Northern Dipper, Three Terraces, Director of Fate, Yellow Emperor carriage, Queen Earth, Grand One, Celestial One, Supreme Palace Enclosure, Hook Array, North Pole, Rain Master, Thunder, Lightning, Minister of Works, Wind Lord, Old Man—62 spirits.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Cheng of Jin established both suburban altars. The heavenly suburb honored sixty-two spirits: assistants to the Five Emperors, the sun and moon, the five planets, the twenty-eight lodges, Literary Glory, the Northern Dipper, the Three Terraces, the Director of Fate, the Yellow Emperor's carriage, Queen Earth, Grand One, Celestial One, the Supreme Palace Enclosure, the Hook Array, the North Pole, the Rain Master, Thunder, Lightning, the Minister of Works, the Wind Lord, and the Old Man.

sentences.zh: 地郊則四十四神，五嶽、四望、四海、四瀆、五湖、五帝之佐、沂山、嶽山、白山、霍山、毉無閭山、蔣山、松江、會稽山、錢唐江、先農凡四十四也。

translations.literal: Earthly suburb then 44 spirits— Five Sacred Mountains, Four Outlooks, Four Seas, Four Watercourses, Five Lakes, Five Emperors' assistants, Mount Yi, Mount Yue, Mount Bai, Mount Huo, Mount Yiwulü, Mount Jiang, Song River, Mount Kuaiji, Qiantang River, First Farmer—in all 44.
translations.idiomatic: The earthly suburb honored forty-four spirits: the Five Sacred Mountains, the Four Outlooks, the Four Seas, the Four Watercourses, the Five Lakes, assistants to the Five Emperors, Mount Yi, Mount Yue, Mount Bai, Mount Huo, Mount Yiwulü, Mount Jiang, the Song River, Mount Kuaiji, the Qiantang River, and the Spirit of Agriculture.

sentences.zh: 江南諸小山，蓋江左所立，猶如漢西京關中小水，皆有祭秩也。

translations.literal: Various small mountains of Jiangnan were probably established by Jiangzuo, like Han Western Capital's small waters within the passes—all have sacrificial ranks.
translations.idiomatic: The lesser mountains of Jiangnan were established after the move south, much as the Western Han assigned sacrificial rank to minor waterways near the capital passes.

sentences.zh: 二郊所秩，官有其注。

translations.literal: What the two suburbs rank, the offices have annotations for.
translations.idiomatic: The roster of spirits for each suburban altar is recorded in the official commentary.

sentences.zh: 宋武帝永初三年九月，司空羨之、尚書令亮等奏曰：「臣聞崇德明祀，百王之令典；

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Song Yongchu year three ninth month, Minister of Works Xianzhi, Director of the Masters of Writing Liang and others memorialized: "We have heard that exalting virtue and illuminating sacrifice is the august canon of the hundred kings;
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of Yongchu 3, Minister of Works Xie Xianzhi, Director of the Masters of Writing Fu Liang, and others submitted: "We have heard that exalting virtue through bright sacrifice is the august canon of every dynasty;

sentences.zh: 憲章天人，自昔之所同。

translations.literal: Taking Heaven and Man as model, from of old what all share.
translations.idiomatic: and that aligning human affairs with Heaven has always been the same principle.

sentences.zh: 雖因革殊時，質文異世，所以本情篤教，其揆一也。

translations.literal: Though change and reform differ by era, substance and ornament differ by age— the reason is honoring the root feeling and sincere teaching; the measure is one.
translations.idiomatic: Forms may change with the age, plain or ornate as the times require, but the root purpose—honoring Heaven and teaching reverence—remains one.

sentences.zh: 伏惟高祖武皇帝允協靈祇，有命自天，弘日靜之勤，立蒸民之極，帝遷明德，光宅八表，太和宣被，玄化遐通。

translations.literal: Respectfully considering Grand Ancestor Emperor Wu accorded with spirits and earthly powers, mandate from Heaven, expanding daily tranquility's diligence, establishing the people's pinnacle; the emperor moved the bright virtue, illuminating the eight directions, great harmony proclaimed and spread, mysterious transformation reaching far.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Ancestor Emperor Wu harmonized with Heaven and Earth and received his mandate from above; through unceasing diligence he established the people's foundation, moved virtue across the realm, spread great harmony, and extended the transforming influence of his rule to the farthest reaches.

sentences.zh: 陛下以聖哲嗣徽，道孚萬國。

translations.literal: Your Majesty with sage wisdom succeeding the emblem, the Way winning over ten thousand states.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty, inheriting this legacy with sage wisdom, has won the loyalty of every state.

sentences.zh: 祭禮久廢，思光鴻烈，饗帝嚴親，今實宜之。

translations.literal: Sacrifice ritual long abandoned; thinking to brighten the great achievement, feasting the Emperor and honoring the parents— now truly suitable.
translations.idiomatic: Sacrificial worship has long lapsed; now is the time to honor Heaven, celebrate your ancestors, and restore the glory of the founding achievement.

sentences.zh: 高祖武皇帝宜配天郊；

translations.literal: Grand Ancestor Emperor Wu is suitable as associate for the Heavenly suburb;
translations.idiomatic: Grand Ancestor Emperor Wu should serve as associate at the heavenly suburban sacrifice;

sentences.zh: 至於地祇之配，雖禮無明文，先代舊章，每所因循，魏、晉故典，足為前式。

translations.literal: As for associate for the Earth Spirit— though ritual has no explicit text, former generations' old regulations were always followed; Wei and Jin former canon suffices as prior model.
translations.idiomatic: For the associate at the earthly sacrifice, though ritual texts are silent, earlier dynasties always established a precedent, and Wei and Jin practice provides a sufficient model.

sentences.zh: 謂武敬皇后宜配北郊。

translations.literal: I say Empress Wu Jing is suitable as associate for the northern suburb.
translations.idiomatic: We propose that Empress Wu Jing serve as associate at the northern suburban sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 蓋述懷以追孝，躋聖敬於無窮，對越兩儀，允洽幽顯者也。

translations.literal: Probably expressing heartfelt remembrance to pursue filial piety, ascending in reverence to the sage without end, facing and surpassing the Two Principles, truly harmonizing the hidden and manifest.
translations.idiomatic: It expresses heartfelt remembrance in pursuit of filial piety, elevating reverence for the sage without end, facing the Two Principles and harmonizing the realms of spirit and flesh.

sentences.zh: 明年孟春，有事於二郊，請宣攝內外，詳依舊典。

translations.literal: Next year in early spring, there will be ritual at the two suburbs— please proclaim throughout inner and outer, following the old canon in detail.
translations.idiomatic: In early spring of the coming year the two suburban sacrifices will be held; we ask that the court be notified throughout and that the old regulations be followed in full.

sentences.zh: 」詔可。

translations.literal: The edict approved.
translations.idiomatic: An edict approved it.

sentences.zh: 晉武帝太康二年冬，有司奏：「三年正月立春祠，時日尚寒，可有司行事。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Jin, winter of Taikang year two, responsible officials memorialized: "In year three, first month, spring establishment sacrifice— the season is still cold; may the responsible officials conduct the ritual."
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of Taikang 2, Emperor Wu of Jin's officials submitted: "The spring-establishment sacrifice in the first month of the third year falls in cold weather; the responsible offices should conduct the rite."

sentences.zh: 」詔曰：「郊祀禮典所重，中間以軍國多事，臨時有所妨廢，故每從奏可。

translations.literal: Edict: "Suburban sacrifice ritual canon is weighty; in the interim because military and state affairs were many, temporarily there were impediments and suspensions— thus each time we followed the memorial's approval.
translations.idiomatic: The edict replied: "The suburban sacrifice is among the weightiest of ritual canons; during the wars we repeatedly suspended it and approved your requests to delegate the rite.

sentences.zh: 自今方外事簡，唯此為大，親奉禋享，固常典也。」

translations.literal: From now external affairs are simple; only this is great— personally performing the smoke offering and feast is the established canon."
translations.idiomatic: From now on external affairs are simpler, and this rite above all demands the emperor's personal presence at the smoke offering and feast."

sentences.zh: 成帝祠南郊，遇雨。

translations.literal: Emperor Cheng performed sacrifice at the southern suburb and encountered rain.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Cheng sacrificed at the southern suburb, rain fell.

sentences.zh: 侍中顧和啟：「宜還。

translations.literal: Attendant Within Gu He submitted: "It is suitable to return.
translations.idiomatic: Attendant Within Gu He submitted: "The procession should turn back.

sentences.zh: 更剋日。

translations.literal: Set another day.
translations.idiomatic: A new date should be chosen."

sentences.zh: 」詔可。

translations.literal: The edict approved.
translations.idiomatic: An edict approved it.

sentences.zh: 漢明帝據月令有五郊迎氣服色之禮，因採元始中故事，兆五郊于洛陽，祭其帝與神，車服各順方色。

translations.literal: Emperor Ming of Han, according to the Monthly Ordinances, had the five-suburb rite of welcoming the seasons with garment colors; adopting precedents from the Yuanshi period, he established the five suburbs at Luoyang, sacrificing to their emperors and spirits, chariots and garments each following the directional color.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming of Han, following the Monthly Ordinances, instituted the five-suburb rite of welcoming the seasons with appropriate colors; adopting Yuanshi-period precedents, he established five suburban altars at Luoyang and sacrificed to their emperors and spirits, with chariots and garments colored according to each direction.

sentences.zh: 魏、晉依之。

translations.literal: Wei and Jin followed this.
translations.idiomatic: Wei and Jin followed the same practice.

sentences.zh: 江左以來，未遑修建。

translations.literal: Since Jiangzuo, there has been no leisure to construct them.
translations.idiomatic: After the move south, the court has had no opportunity to build them.

sentences.zh: 宋孝武大明五年四月庚子，詔曰：「昔文德在周，明堂崇祀；

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowu of Song, Daming year five fourth month gengzi, edict: "Formerly civil virtue was in Zhou, and the Bright Hall honored sacrifice;
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of Daming 5, Emperor Xiaowu issued an edict: "When civil virtue flourished in Zhou, the Bright Hall was the seat of supreme worship;

sentences.zh: 高烈惟漢，汶邑斯尊。

translations.literal: high merit was in Han, and Wenshi was thus honored.
translations.idiomatic: and when Han rose on great merit, Wenyi was honored in the same way.

sentences.zh: 所以職祭罔諐，氣令斯正，鴻名稱首，濟世飛聲。

translations.literal: Thus sacrificial duties were without error, seasonal commands were correct, the great name was foremost, and benefit to the age resounded far.
translations.idiomatic: Through such worship the seasons were kept true, the great name was exalted, and benefit to the age resounded far.

sentences.zh: 朕皇考太祖文皇帝功耀洞元，聖靈昭俗，內穆四門，仁濟羣品，外薄八荒，威憺殊俗，南腦勁越，西髓剛戎。

translations.literal: Our late father Grand Ancestor Emperor Wen, merit shining through the primal void, sage spirit illuminating custom, inwardly harmonizing the four gates, benevolence reaching all ranks, outwardly pressing the eight directions, awe calming distant peoples, the south submitting with tribute, the west yielding with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Our late father, Grand Ancestor Emperor Wen, whose merit shone through the primal void and whose sage spirit illuminated custom, harmonized the realm within, brought benevolence to every rank, pressed outward to the eight directions, and awed distant peoples into submission.

sentences.zh: 裁禮興稼穡之根，張樂協四氣之紀。

translations.literal: Regulating ritual and raising the roots of agriculture; spreading music and harmonizing the four seasons' records.
translations.idiomatic: He regulated ritual and raised the roots of agriculture, spread music and harmonized the records of the four seasons.

sentences.zh: 匡飾墳序，引無題之外；

translations.literal: Adorning and ordering the ancestral sequence, drawing in what lay beyond the untitled;
translations.idiomatic: He adorned the ancestral order and drew in what lay beyond the untitled;

sentences.zh: 旌延寶臣，盡盛德之範。

translations.literal: extending banners to worthy ministers, exhausting the models of utmost virtue.
translations.idiomatic: he extended honor to worthy ministers and embodied the fullest models of virtue.

sentences.zh: 訓深劭農，政高刑厝。

translations.literal: Instruction deep in urging agriculture, governance high in setting aside punishment.
translations.idiomatic: His instruction urged agriculture; his governance set punishment aside.

sentences.zh: 萬物棣通，百神薦祉。

translations.literal: The ten thousand things flowed in harmony, the hundred spirits presented blessings.
translations.idiomatic: The ten thousand things flowed in harmony, and the hundred spirits presented blessings.

sentences.zh: 動協天度，下沿地德。

translations.literal: Movement accorded with Heaven's measure, below following Earth's virtue.
translations.idiomatic: His movement accorded with Heaven's measure and followed Earth's virtue below.

sentences.zh: 故精緯上靈，動殖下瑞，諸侯軌道，河溓海夷。

translations.literal: Thus essences and threads of the upper spirits, movements and growth of lower auspices, feudal lords kept the Way, rivers clear and seas calm.
translations.idiomatic: Essences of the upper spirits and auspicious growth below responded; feudal lords kept the Way, and the realm from river to sea lay at peace.

sentences.zh: 朕仰憑洪烈，入子萬姓，皇天降祐，迄將一紀。

translations.literal: I respectfully rely on the great achievement, entering as son to the myriad people; Heaven and Earth send blessing, nearly reaching one full cycle.
translations.idiomatic: I rely on this great achievement as ruler of the myriad people; Heaven and Earth have blessed my reign for nearly a full cycle.

sentences.zh: 思奉揚休德，永播無窮。

translations.literal: Thinking to uphold and spread the beautiful virtue, forever broadcasting without end.
translations.idiomatic: I wish to uphold and spread that beautiful virtue forever.

sentences.zh: 便可詳考姬典，經始明堂，宗祀先靈，式配上帝，誠敬克展，幽顯咸秩。

translations.literal: Then may one examine in detail the Ji canon, begin the Bright Hall, ancestral worship to the former spirits, form matching the Supreme Lord, sincerity and reverence fully displayed, hidden and manifest all in order.
translations.idiomatic: Let the Ji canon be examined in detail, the Bright Hall begun, the former spirits worshipped, and the Supreme Lord matched in form—sincerity and reverence fully displayed, the hidden and manifest all in order.

sentences.zh: 惟懷永遠，感慕崩心。

translations.literal: Only thoughts reaching far, moved to grief by the departed heart.
translations.idiomatic: My thoughts reach far, and my heart is moved to grief for the departed."

sentences.zh: 」有司奏：「伏尋明堂辟雍，制無定文，經記參差，傳說乖舛。

translations.literal: Responsible officials memorialized: "Respectfully seeking, Bright Hall and Imperial Academy have no fixed text in the regulations; classics and records differ, transmitted explanations contradict.
translations.idiomatic: The responsible officials submitted: "The Bright Hall and Imperial Academy have no fixed design in the regulations; the classics disagree and transmitted explanations contradict one another.

sentences.zh: 名儒通哲，各事所見，或以為名異實同，或以為名實皆異。

translations.literal: Famous scholars and penetrating sages each follow what they see— some consider the names different but the substance the same, some consider both names and substance different.
translations.idiomatic: Famous scholars and penetrating sages each follow their own view—some hold the names differ but the substance is the same, others that both name and substance differ.

sentences.zh: 自漢暨晉，莫之能辨。

translations.literal: From Han through Jin, none could distinguish.
translations.idiomatic: From Han through Jin, none could settle the question.

sentences.zh: 周書云，清廟明堂路寢同制。

translations.literal: Documents of Zhou say the Clear Temple, Bright Hall, and Road Chamber share one form.
translations.idiomatic: The Documents of Zhou state that the Clear Temple, Bright Hall, and Road Chamber share one form.

sentences.zh: 鄭玄注禮，義生於斯。

translations.literal: Zheng Xuan annotating the Rites, meaning arises from this.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Xuan's commentary on the Rites derives its meaning from this passage.

sentences.zh: 諸儒又云明堂在國之陽，丙巳之地，三里之內。

translations.literal: Various scholars also say the Bright Hall is in the state's south, at the bingji position, within three li.
translations.idiomatic: Other scholars place the Bright Hall south of the capital at the bingji position, within three li.

sentences.zh: 至於室宇堂个，戶牖達向，世代湮緬，難得該詳。

translations.literal: As for chambers, halls, and bays, doors, windows, and facing directions— generations obscure and distant, hard to obtain complete detail.
translations.idiomatic: The layout of chambers, bays, doors, windows, and orientations has grown obscure over the generations, and complete detail is hard to recover.

sentences.zh: 晉侍中裴頠，西都碩學，考詳前載，未能制定。

translations.literal: Jin Attendant Within Pei Wei, Western Capital eminent scholar, examining former records in detail, could not fix the design.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Wei of Jin, Attendant Within and eminent scholar of the Western Capital, examined earlier records in detail but could not fix the design.

sentences.zh: 以為尊祖配天，其義明著，廟宇之制，理據未分，直可為殿，以崇嚴祀。

translations.literal: He considered honoring the ancestor and matching Heaven— the meaning is clearly established; the temple structure's rationale is not yet divided— one may directly make a hall to exalt solemn sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: He held that honoring the ancestor and matching Heaven was clearly established in meaning, while the temple structure remained unsettled; a hall could be built at once to exalt solemn worship.

sentences.zh: 其餘雜碎，一皆除之。

translations.literal: The remaining miscellaneous matters— all remove them.
translations.idiomatic: All other miscellaneous details should be set aside.

sentences.zh: 參詳鄭玄之注，差有準據；

translations.literal: Examining Zheng Xuan's annotations in detail, there is some standard basis;
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Xuan's annotations, examined in detail, provide some standard basis;

sentences.zh: 裴頠之奏，竊謂可安。

translations.literal: Pei Wei's memorial— I consider it can be settled.
translations.idiomatic: and Pei Wei's memorial, in my view, can be adopted.

sentences.zh: 國學之南，地實丙巳，爽塏平暢，足以營建。

translations.literal: South of the National Academy, the ground is truly at bingji, open and level and smooth— sufficient to construct.
translations.idiomatic: South of the National Academy the ground lies truly at bingji, open, level, and smooth— sufficient for construction.

sentences.zh: 其墻宇規範，宜擬則太廟，唯十有二間，以應朞數。

translations.literal: Its wall and chamber standards should take the Grand Temple as model, only twelve bays to correspond to the cycle number.
translations.idiomatic: Its walls and chambers should follow the Grand Temple as model, with twelve bays to correspond to the cycle number.

sentences.zh: 依漢汶上圖儀，設五帝位，太祖文皇帝對饗。

translations.literal: Following Han Wenshang diagram protocol, set the Five Emperors' positions, with Grand Ancestor Emperor Wen facing in the feast.
translations.idiomatic: Following Han Wenshang diagram protocol, set the Five Emperors' positions, with Grand Ancestor Emperor Wen facing them at the feast.

sentences.zh: 祭皇天上帝，雖為差降，至於三載恭祀，理不容異。

translations.literal: Sacrificing to August Heaven the Supreme Lord, though there is some lowering in rank, as for the three-year reverent sacrifice, by principle there can be no difference.
translations.idiomatic: Sacrifice to August Heaven the Supreme Lord involves some lowering in rank, but the three-year reverent ceremony cannot logically differ.

sentences.zh: 自郊徂宮，亦宜共日。

translations.literal: From the suburb returning to the palace, it is also suitable to be the same day.
translations.idiomatic: The return from the suburb to the palace should also fall on the same day.

sentences.zh: 禮記郊以特牲，詩稱明堂羊牛，吉蠲雖同，質文殊典。

translations.literal: Book of Rites: suburb uses special victim; Odes call Bright Hall sheep and ox— auspicious purification though the same, substance and ornament differ in canon.
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Rites prescribes a special victim for the suburb; the Odes speak of sheep and ox for the Bright Hall—purification is the same, but substance and ornament differ by canon.

sentences.zh: 且郊有燔柴，堂無禋燎，則鼎俎彝簋，一依廟禮。

translations.literal: Moreover the suburb has burning firewood; the hall has no smoke offering— then tripods, stands, and ritual vessels all follow temple ritual.
translations.idiomatic: The suburb includes burning firewood, but the hall has no smoke offering; tripods, stands, and ritual vessels should all follow temple ritual.

sentences.zh: 班行百司，搜材簡工，權置起部尚書、將作大匠，量物商程，剋今秋繕立。

translations.literal: Deploy the hundred offices, seek materials and select craftsmen; provisionally appoint Director of the Construction Department and Grand Master of Works, measure materials and calculate the schedule, set this autumn for construction.
translations.idiomatic: Deploy the hundred offices, gather materials and select craftsmen, provisionally appoint the Director of the Construction Department and Grand Master of Works, measure materials and calculate the schedule, and set construction for this autumn.

sentences.zh: 」乃依頠議，但作大殿屋雕畫而已，無古三十六戶七十二牖之制。

translations.literal: Then they followed Pei's proposal, but only made a great hall building with carved painting— no ancient thirty-six doors seventy-two windows form.
translations.idiomatic: They followed Pei's proposal but built only a great hall with carved decoration—without the ancient form of thirty-six doors and seventy-two windows.

sentences.zh: 六年正月，南郊還，世祖親奉明堂，祠祭五時之帝，以文皇帝配，是用鄭玄議也。

translations.literal: Sixth year first month, returning from southern suburb, Shizu personally performed at the Bright Hall, sacrificing to the Five Seasons' Emperors, with Emperor Wen as associate— this used Zheng Xuan's proposal.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the sixth year, returning from the southern suburb, Emperor Shizu personally worshipped at the Bright Hall, sacrificing to the Five Seasons' Emperors with Emperor Wen as associate—following Zheng Xuan's proposal.

sentences.zh: 官有其注。

translations.literal: The offices have annotations for this.
translations.idiomatic: The offices have annotations recording this.

sentences.zh: 大明五年九月甲子，有司奏：「南郊祭用三牛。

translations.literal: Daming year five ninth month jiazi, responsible officials memorialized: "Southern suburb sacrifice uses three oxen.
translations.idiomatic: On jiazi day of the ninth month in Daming 5, the responsible officials submitted: "The southern suburban sacrifice uses three oxen.

sentences.zh: 廟四時祠六室用二牛。

translations.literal: Temple four-seasons sacrifice six chambers uses two oxen.
translations.idiomatic: The temple's four-season sacrifice in six chambers uses two oxen.

sentences.zh: 明堂肇建，祠五帝，太祖文皇帝配，未詳祭用幾牛？

translations.literal: Bright Hall newly established, sacrificing to the Five Emperors, with Grand Ancestor Emperor Wen as associate— not yet clear how many oxen for sacrifice?"
translations.idiomatic: The Bright Hall has been newly established to sacrifice to the Five Emperors with Grand Ancestor Emperor Wen as associate—how many oxen should be used?"

sentences.zh: 」太學博士司馬興之議：「案鄭玄注禮記大傳稱：『孝經郊祀后稷以配天，配靈威仰也。

translations.literal: Erudite of the Imperial Academy Sima Xingzhi argued: "Considering Zheng Xuan's annotation on the Great Tradition in the Book of Rites: 'The Classic of Filial Piety: at the suburb sacrifice Hou Ji as associate for Heaven, associating with Spiritual Brilliance and Ascent.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Xingzhi, Erudite of the Imperial Academy, argued: "Zheng Xuan's annotation on the Great Tradition in the Book of Rites states: 'The Classic of Filial Piety: at the suburban sacrifice Hou Ji accompanies Heaven, associating with Spiritual Brilliance and Ascent.

sentences.zh: 宗祀文王於明堂，以配上帝，配五帝也。

translations.literal: Ancestral worship of King Wen at the Bright Hall, as associate for the Supreme Lord, associating with the Five Emperors.'
translations.idiomatic: Ancestral worship of King Wen at the Bright Hall accompanies the Supreme Lord, associating with the Five Emperors.'

sentences.zh: 』夫五帝司方，位殊功一，牲牢之用，理無差降。

translations.literal: The Five Emperors govern directions, positions differ but merit is one— sacrificial victims' use, by principle has no lowering in rank.
translations.idiomatic: The Five Emperors govern the directions; their positions differ but their merit is one—sacrificial victims should not be reduced in rank.

sentences.zh: 太祖文皇帝躬成天地，則道兼覆載；

translations.literal: Grand Ancestor Emperor Wen personally completed Heaven and Earth— then the Way encompasses covering and bearing;
translations.idiomatic: Grand Ancestor Emperor Wen personally completed Heaven and Earth—his Way encompasses covering and bearing;

sentences.zh: 左右羣生，則化洽四氣。

translations.literal: left and right all living beings— then transformation harmonizes the four seasons.
translations.idiomatic: and left and right all living beings—his transformation harmonizes the four seasons.

sentences.zh: 祖、宗之稱，不足彰無窮之美；

translations.literal: Titles of ancestor and temple— insufficient to display boundless beauty;
translations.idiomatic: Titles of ancestor and temple are insufficient to display boundless beauty;

sentences.zh: 金石之音，未能播勳烈之盛。

translations.literal: sounds of metal and stone— unable to broadcast the splendor of achievement.
translations.idiomatic: and sounds of metal and stone cannot broadcast the splendor of his achievement.

sentences.zh: 故明堂聿修，聖心所以昭玄極；

translations.literal: Thus the Bright Hall was urgently built— the sage heart thereby displays the dark pole;
translations.idiomatic: Thus the Bright Hall was built—the sage heart thereby displays the dark pole;

sentences.zh: 汎配宗廟，先儒所以得禮情。

translations.literal: broadly matching the ancestral temple— former scholars thereby obtain ritual sentiment.
translations.idiomatic: and broadly matching the ancestral temple—former scholars thereby express true ritual sentiment.

sentences.zh: 愚管所見，謂宜用六牛。

translations.literal: My humble view considers it suitable to use six oxen.
translations.idiomatic: In my humble view, six oxen should be used.

sentences.zh: 」博士虞龢議：「祀帝之名雖五，而所生之實常一。

translations.literal: Erudite Yu He argued: "The names of the emperors worshipped are though five, yet the substance of what they generate is constantly one.
translations.idiomatic: Yu He, Erudite, argued: "Though five emperors are worshipped by name, the substance they generate is constantly one.

sentences.zh: 五德之帝，迭有休王，各有所司，故有五室。

translations.literal: The Five Virtues' Emperors in turn had resting kings, each governing what they oversee— thus there are five chambers.
translations.idiomatic: The Five Virtues' Emperors in turn had resting kings, each governing its domain—hence there are five chambers.

sentences.zh: 宗祀所主，要隨其王而饗焉。

translations.literal: What ancestral worship chiefly honors must follow whichever king and feast accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: Ancestral worship must follow whichever king is chiefly honored and feast accordingly.

sentences.zh: 主一配一，合用二牛。

translations.literal: One chief, one associate— jointly suitable to use two oxen.
translations.idiomatic: One chief deity and one associate—two oxen are appropriate.

sentences.zh: 」祠部郎顏奐議：「祀之為義，並五帝以為言。

translations.literal: Section Director of Sacrifices Yan Huan argued: "The meaning of sacrifice— all take the Five Emperors as the statement.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Huan, Section Director of Sacrifices, argued: "Sacrifice, in its meaning, always speaks of the Five Emperors.

sentences.zh: 帝雖云五，牲牢之用，謂不應過郊祭廟祀。

translations.literal: Though the emperors are said to be five, sacrificial victims' use— I say should not exceed suburban sacrifice and temple sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: Though five emperors are named, the sacrificial victims used should not exceed those for suburban sacrifice and temple sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 宜用二牛。」

translations.literal: It is suitable to use two oxen."
translations.idiomatic: Two oxen should be used."

sentences.zh: 明帝泰始七年十月庚子，有司奏：「來年正月十八日，祠明堂。

translations.literal: Emperor Ming, Taishi year seven tenth month gengzi, responsible officials memorialized: "Next year first month eighteenth day, sacrifice at the Bright Hall.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of Taishi 7, Emperor Ming's officials submitted: "On the eighteenth day of the first month next year, sacrifice will be performed at the Bright Hall.

sentences.zh: 尋舊南郊與明堂同日，並告太廟。

translations.literal: Seeking the old practice, southern suburb and Bright Hall same day, both announcing to the Grand Temple.
translations.idiomatic: Under the old practice, the southern suburb and Bright Hall fell on the same day, and both were announced to the Grand Temple.

sentences.zh: 未審今祀明堂，復告與不？

translations.literal: Not yet examined: now sacrificing at the Bright Hall— again announce or not?"
translations.idiomatic: It is not yet clear whether, when sacrificing at the Bright Hall, the Grand Temple should again be notified."

sentences.zh: 」祠部郎王延秀議：「案鄭玄云：『郊者祭天之名，上帝者，天之別名也。

translations.literal: Section Director of Sacrifices Wang Yanxiu argued: "Considering Zheng Xuan: 'Suburb means the name of sacrificing to Heaven; Supreme Lord is Heaven's other name.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yanxiu, Section Director of Sacrifices, argued: "Zheng Xuan states: 'Suburb is the name for sacrificing to Heaven; Supreme Lord is Heaven's other name.

sentences.zh: 神無二主，故明堂異處，以避后稷。

translations.literal: Spirits have no two masters— thus the Bright Hall is at a different place, to avoid Hou Ji.'
translations.idiomatic: Spirits have no two masters—thus the Bright Hall stands elsewhere, to avoid Hou Ji.'

sentences.zh: 』謹尋郊宗二祀，既名殊實同，至於應告，不容有異。
